messages.content: How can I compute edit distance with only O(min(m,n)) extra memory? Illustrate with kitten and sitting.

message.content:
Use the standard DP recurrence, but keep only one row (or two rows) of the DP table. Since edit distance is symmetric, make the shorter string the column dimension. Then the working array has length `min(m,n)+1`.

Let `A = "kitten"` (shorter, length 6) and `B = "sitting"` (longer, length 7). Define

\[
dp[j] = \text{edit distance between } A[:j] \text{ and } B[:i]
\]

after processing the first `i` characters of `B`.

Update rule:

\[
dp[j] = \min
\begin{cases}
\text{old } dp[j] + 1 & \text{delete/insert} \\
dp[j-1] + 1 & \text{insert/delete} \\
\text{old } dp[j-1] + \text{cost} & \text{match/substitute}
\end{cases}
\]

where `cost = 0` if `A[j-1] == B[i-1]`, else `1`.

One-row implementation:

```python
def edit_distance(a, b):
    if len(a) > len(b):
        a, b = b, a          # a is the shorter string
    m = len(a)
    dp = list(range(m + 1))  # dp[j] = distance to a[:j]

    for i, ch in enumerate(b, 1):
        prev = dp[0]
        dp[0] = i
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            old = dp[j]
            cost = 0 if a[j - 1] == ch else 1
            dp[j] = min(
                old + 1,          # delete/insert
                dp[j - 1] + 1,    # insert/delete
                prev + cost       # match/substitute
            )
            prev = old

    return dp[m]
```

For `kitten` and `sitting`, the rolling DP rows are:

| `B` prefix | `dp[0]` | `dp[1]` | `dp[2]` | `dp[3]` | `dp[4]` | `dp[5]` | `dp[6]` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `""` | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| `s` | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| `si` | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| `sit` | 3 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| `sitt` | 4 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| `sitti` | 5 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| `sittin` | 6 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| `sitting` | 7 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 4 | **3** |

The final value is `dp[6] = 3`, so the edit distance is **3**.

One optimal edit sequence is:

```text
kitten
sitten   # substitute k -> s
sittin   # substitute e -> i
sitting  # insert g
```

The table above is only for illustration; the algorithm stores just one row of length `min(m,n)+1`, so extra memory is `O(min(m,n))`.

def edit_distance(a,b):
    if len(a) > len(b):
        a,b = b,a
    m = len(a)

            old = dp[j]
            cost = 0 if a[j-1] == ch else 1
            dp[j] = min(old + 1, dp[j-1] + 1, prev + cost)
            prev = old
    return dp[m]
